task.title: P6-127 residue: tree/payload freshness window, CollectionPath fallback, bump encapsulation, restore bump, toast-timing flake risk
task.description:
Residue from P6-127 adversarial review (2026-08-12), all minor/transient:

1. Tree-overrides-fresher-payload window: after a delete/reparent, both tree.refetch() and the content_revision payload refetch fire; if the payload lands first, tree-derived folder rows (collection.rs ~:245,:1546) keep the deleted/moved child visible (linking to a dead id) until the tree round trip completes. Self-healing. Consider preferring the fresher source (e.g. stamp TreeFacts with the tree fetch generation) if it ever bites.
2. CollectionPath (collection.rs ~:910) still falls back to the payload name for the current node — not converted to tree_facts; a rename updates the h1 but the breadcrumb tail lags until the next payload refetch.
3. TreeManage.revision/content_revision are pub RwSignals while the bump helpers own the classification — a future caller can open-code a bump and bypass it. Consider making the signals private with read accessors.
4. restore_collection (recently_deleted.rs ~:151) refetches the tree but bumps neither counter (pre-existing before P6-127); if a restore can change a viewed page's rows, it should bump content_revision — verify and fix or document why not.
5. e2e "rename mid-toast leaves Undo working" test: the whole rename-dialog interaction must fit inside the 5s toast lifetime — load-sensitive flake risk (guarded: fails rather than passes vacuously). Consider an API-level undo assertion fallback if it flakes in practice.
